classification.difficultyReason: The context gives r = 1/2 directly from 'halves every day', and parts a to d are a scaffolded run of 20, 10, 5 and 0.625. The hardest demand is part e. The student must generalise to 20(1/2)^k and handle the offset between days elapsed and term number. Here the exponent is just k, so no a_{k+1} indexing needs to be reasoned out. This is a little harder than p8-q8, which asks for the ratio and a formula from listed terms. It is easier than A3, which needs a modelled two-step expression and an algebraic fraction.
